title: Canonical Data Model
description: The formal, source-independent definition of the canonical data model: which labels exist, what values they take, and why. This file defines the model itself, not how any particular source maps into it -- that mapping is hand-written metric_relabel_configs in demo/src/prometheus/prometheus-config.yaml, which enriches series with exactly these labels. See ../README.md for the label reference in prose and the reasoning behind each one.

cdm_metric.description: The canonical identity to query by, in place of a renamed metric name (__name__ is left exactly as the source emits it -- see ../README.md's 'enrichment, not a rename'). Query with a name-less selector, e.g. {cdm_metric="requests_total", cdm_service=~"..."}.

cdm_source.description: Which source type produced this series -- one value per relabeling section in prometheus-config.yaml, so the source type is queryable/selectable instead of only living in a comment.

cdm_service.description: The entity this series is about. Renamed from whatever the source calls it (service_name for spanmetrics, a static value derived from instance for Envoy/Grafana).

env.description: Deployment environment, from deployment.environment.name (or the older deployment.environment). Not cdm_-prefixed: deployment.environment.name is already a near-universal ecosystem convention. Not populated in this demo (single environment).

cdm_request_type.description: What kind of request. Derived from which semantic-convention attribute is present on the source, not from a fixed source-specific value -- this is what lets the same query work across HTTP, gRPC and future sources without listing them all.

cdm_request_context.description: Which request/operation -- an HTTP route, an RPC method, a DB operation, falling back to whatever the source's own operation identifier is (e.g. a span name) when nothing more specific exists.

cdm_direction.description: Which side of a call this series represents, from OTel's span.kind (SERVER/CONSUMER vs. CLIENT/PRODUCER) or the source's equivalent. Without this, summing a service's inbound and outbound calls together double-counts the same logical request from both ends.

cdm_status.description: Collapsed from whatever the source's own error signal is (span status, HTTP status class, response code class, ...).

cdm_unit.description: The unit a request_duration series' value is actually in. Not normalized away: relabeling can rewrite labels but never a sample's value, so a source reporting milliseconds can't be silently forced to look like seconds. Queries that aggregate across cdm_unit values must account for that explicitly.
